subject: Astra Biotech — Hosted API: data residency, retention & deletion Qs
messages:
From: Emma Wells <emma.wells@astrabiotech.com>

Cc: procurement@astrabiotech.com, security@astrabiotech.com
Date: Fri, 03 Aug 2028 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Initial Qs on data residency + retention for Hosted API

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team at Astra appreciated the performance numbers. Procurement and security asked me to follow up with a short questionnaire focused specifically on data residency, logs/retention, and deletion workflows for the hosted API. Our concerns are EU-only processing and demonstrable erasure for audit.

Can you confirm the following?
1) Can requests and derived artifacts (embeddings, logs, session state) be restricted to EU regions only (no replication outside the EU)?
2) What are default retention windows for request logs, full request/response payloads, and model-level caches?
3) If we request customer-initiated deletion (legal/user erasure), what is the end-to-end timeline and evidence you provide?
4) Are backups or disaster recovery copies retained in other regions, and how are they purged?

We'd like answers to present to our DPO and to include in the SOW. If useful, happy to take a 30-min sync.

Best,
Emma
Emma Wells
Head of IT Security, Astra Biotech

Team — forwarding Astra's questionnaire. They want EU-only processing, retention windows, and deletion evidence. I drafted a short answers doc attached but need final sign-off on the specifics below before I send to Emma.

Key points to confirm:
- EU-only tenancy option for hosted API (no cross-region replication) — is this fully supported today for production customers? Which regions (Frankfurt/Amsterdam)?
- Retention defaults vs. configurable retention per-customer (logs, request bodies, embeddings, KV/prefix caches). We should be explicit about separate buckets/TTL and how long forensic logs live.
- Backup/DR replication behavior and purge guarantees (esp. snapshot/backup retention in multi-region failover).
- Deletion flow: from request to confirmation, and whether we provide a signed erasure certificate / audit log entry.

Marcus — can you confirm backup behavior for EU-only tenants?
Soojin — please advise on the legal text we can include for SOW/Vendor attestation.
Karthik — any product caveats (e.g., cached prefixes in inference nodes) to call out?

Thanks,

From: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
To: jonas.weber@redwood.ai, soojin.lee@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 03 Aug 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Initial Qs on data residency + retention for Hosted API

All — answers below (high level). I'll attach a short diagram and retention table. We should be conservative for Astra and offer EU-only tenancy with the following characteristics:

1) EU-only processing: yes. Production tenants can be provisioned in a strict EU tenancy in the Amsterdam and Frankfurt regions (eu-west-1, eu-central-1). No active replication of customer request/response payloads or embeddings to non-EU regions under the EU-only tenancy. Some metadata (billing meter points / aggregated anonymized telemetry) may be stored in the control plane in the US for scale; we can include an optional control-plane-data residency addendum.

2) Retention defaults (hosted API):
- API request/response payloads: default 30 days, configurable down to 0 days on request (zero-retention option).
- Request logs (ingestion metadata, status, error traces): default 90 days; configurable to 30/90/180.
- Embeddings/derived artifacts: default 365 days; configurable to 90/365 or delete-on-request. Note: embeddings used for cache/semantic search can be scoped to customer-managed indexes.
- Model KV/prefix caches: ephemeral (default 24 hours) and not persisted to long-term storage; cache content is treated as ephemeral inference state and is not included in backups.

3) Backups & DR:
- Automated backups of persistent stores (index snapshots, long-term logs) are retained in the same region by default. For EU-only tenancy, backups are stored in EU S3/Blob storage with cross-region replication disabled.
- For customers who opt into cross-region DR, replication targets are explicitly configured and documented; absence of opt-in = no cross-region copies.
- Snapshots are retained per the retention table; deleted snapshots are tombstoned and then wiped within the next backup cycle (typically 7 days), with secure deletion policies applied.

4) Deletion / erasure process:
- On receipt of a verified erasure request (via the support portal + DPO contact), we begin the deletion workflow within 24 hours.
- Persistent artifacts (request/response payloads, embeddings, indexes) are queued for immediate deletion and removed from live disks within a maximum of 72 hours.
- Backups and snapshots containing the data are identified; tombstoned snapshots are scheduled for wipe and purged within 30 days, with accelerations available for POA in certain contracts.
- Evidence: we provide a deletion report (timestamped manifest of deleted object keys/IDs) and an audit entry showing workflow completion. For higher assurance, we can provide a signed erasure certificate (PDF) as part of the SOW.

Caveats:
- If the customer elects to use our hosted anonymized telemetry features, aggregated metrics may persist outside the customer tenancy but are irreversibly de-identified.
- Short-lived caches on inference shards (KV caches) might have transient copies in memory; these are not persisted and are cleared on shard restart.

I'll attach the diagram (Redwood_DataResidency_Diagram.png) and the retention spreadsheet. Happy to refine wording for the SOW.

Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Initial Qs on data residency + retention for Hosted API

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. Per Marcus and team, answers below. I've summarized the commitments we'd include in the SOW and attached the retention table + diagram for your review.

Short answers (executive summary):
1) EU-only processing: Yes. We can provision a strict EU tenancy (Amsterdam or Frankfurt). No customer payloads or embeddings will be replicated outside the EU unless you explicitly opt into cross-region DR. Control-plane telemetry for billing/scale may be retained outside the EU; we can add a control-plane residency addendum.

2) Retention defaults & options:
- API request/response payloads: default 30 days; can be set to 0 (no retention) for strict data minimization needs.
- Request logs: default 90 days; configurable.
- Derived artifacts (embeddings, indexes): default 365 days; configurable and can be deleted on request.
- Ephemeral inference state / KV caches: ephemeral (24h) and not persisted to backups.

3) Deletion timeline & evidence:
- Deletion workflow starts within 24 hours of a verified request.
- Live data removal from the tenancy: up to 72 hours.
- Backups/snapshots purge window: up to 30 days (faster purge negotiable in SOW).
- We will provide a deletion manifest and a timestamped audit entry; signed erasure certificates are available as a contract addendum.

4) Backups & DR:
- EU-only tenants keep backups in-region by default; cross-region replication is opt-in.
- Deleted snapshots are tombstoned and securely wiped inside the configured purge window.

Attachments: Redwood_DataResidency_Diagram.png, HostedAPI_Retention_Table.xlsx, Redwood_QA_Answers_v1.pdf

Next steps: can you confirm whether Astra requires a 0-day payload retention option and whether the DPO needs the signed erasure certificate included in the SOW? If helpful, we can lock these items in a 30-min call this week.

Best,
Jonas Weber
